newsitem.title: GREECE: GREEK STOCKS FALL SHARPLY, BELOW 1600 PTS.
newsitem.headline: GREEK STOCKS FALL SHARPLY, BELOW 1600 PTS.

text.p: Greek shares were down 3.0 percent, below the 1,600 support level in mid-session, unnerved by inflation concerns, firmer interbank rates and a plunge in bond prices.
Traders said market sentiment had been hurt by a lower-than-expected May inflation figure and concerns of a tougher course for the CPI in the second half of the year.
May inflation eased to 5.4 percent year-on-year from 5.9 percent in April while the market had been expecting a figure closer to 5.1-5.2 percent.
"Market psychology has been hurt by these developments but we are not witnessing a sell-off. Volume is not particularly heavy," said Alexis Panagiotopoulos, a broker at Intersec.
